title: Composite: one interface for parts and wholes
summary: A File and a Folder both answer size(). A folder sums whatever its children answer, so nesting works at any depth and callers never check which one they hold.
code: # Files and folders answer the same size(), so callers never check which one they hold.
return sum(child.size() for child in self.children)
triggers: a tree of parts and wholes where callers want one operation on a single item or a whole group
recursive structures: folders and files, menus and submenus, org charts, nested expressions
prompts: A drawing app lets users group shapes, and groups can hold other groups. Moving or measuring a group must work exactly like moving or measuring a single shape.
An org chart rolls up salary cost: a manager's cost includes everyone below them at any depth, while an individual's cost is just their own salary.
invariant: File and Folder answer the same size(); a folder's answer is the sum of its children's answers, at any depth.
mantra: Leaves answer; groups ask their children.
pitfalls: isinstance checks in the folder or the caller defeat the pattern; give leaf and group the same method.
Call child.size(), not child.bytes, or nested folders count as nothing.
Don't store an attribute named like a method: self.size = size would hide size().

anchors.name: File system
anchors.trick: Folder.size() sums its children; File.size() returns its bytes.

anchors.name: Restaurant menu
anchors.trick: Menus hold items and submenus; print or price the whole tree with one call.

mutations.replacement: return sum(child.bytes for child in self.children if isinstance(child, File))
mutations.explanation: Counts only the files directly inside; nested folders add nothing because the folder stopped asking its children.
Returns the child, so a chained add() puts the next item inside it, or fails on a file.
